                    ### Question
                    A 35-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of progressive fatigue, shortness of breath, and pain in her knees and ankles. Her temperature is 37.6°C (99.7°F). Physical examination shows mild hepatomegaly and tender, red nodules on her shins. There are purple, indurated lesions on her nose, nasolabial fold, and cheeks. A biopsy of the liver shows scattered aggregations of multinucleated giant cells with cytoplasmic inclusions and eosinophilic, needle-shaped structures arranged in a star-like pattern. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Sarcoidosis
opb. Systemic lupus erythematosus
opc. Hypereosinophilic syndrome
opd. Hemochromatosis
ope. Serum sickness

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of progressive fatigue, shortness of breath, knee and ankle pain, fever, mild hepatomegaly, tender red nodules on shins, purple indurated lesions on the nose and cheeks, along with the biopsy findings of multinucleated giant cells with cytoplasmic inclusions and eosinophilic, needle-shaped structures in a star-like pattern, are most indicative of Churg-Strauss syndrome (Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis) rather than Hypereosinophilic syndrome. This conclusion is supported by the evidence paths related to giant cells, inclusion bodies, and abnormal nucleoli, which align with the characteristic histopathological features of Churg-Strauss syndrome.
